vibe_coder_test.note: The first attempt in this app failed to connect because .mcp.json launched the server with the system python3, which has no fastmcp; the vibe coder then started the server itself, which I did not count as evidence. After .mcp.json was changed to .venv/bin/python, a new session connected and called the tools directly (above). The three tools take no ticket id; 101/102/103 only label which ticket each check is for.

supporting_portkey_test.description: Earlier automated check (python3 mcp_smoke_test.py): a gpt-6-luna agent on Portkey connected through the same .mcp.json and chose and called each tool itself; every output was compared with the database.
supporting_portkey_test.note: These outputs were checked against data/campus_customs_new.db at run_at, before any ticket was run. The submitted database is the state after Problem 9: rent for lease 1 was paid, so get_lease_rent_due(1) now returns next_due 2026-10-02 and days_until_due 32. The other two outputs (CC-TEE-WHITE S qty 0; CC-HOOD-NAVY cost $22.00 / list $58.00) still match.

results.prompt: Ticket 101: Tauhid Zaman wants one CC-TEE-WHITE in size S. Use the campus-customs MCP server to check whether that size is in stock.
results.model_answer: CC-TEE-WHITE in size S is out of stock (0 on hand).

db_check.sql: SELECT qty AS qty_on_hand, location FROM inventory WHERE sku='CC-TEE-WHITE' AND size='S'

results.prompt: Ticket 102 is a rent notice for lease 1. Use the campus-customs MCP server to look up the landlord, monthly rent, and next due date.

db_check.sql: SELECT landlord, monthly_rent, next_due FROM leases WHERE id=1
